g.text: WHERE DOES THE CHANGE IN RESEARCH–BURDEN MISMATCH COME FROM?
LMIC research, 2010–2012 → 2021–2023, compared with a fixed 2021–2023 DALY reference. Disease contributions add to their
level-1 group; the groups add to the overall change.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.5px; font-family: 'Arial'; text-anchor: start; fill: #252721

g.text: Overall mismatch: 32.76% → 32.76%; change +0.004 percentage points (95% interval -4.55 to +3.45).
Mismatch is total variation distance: ½ × Σ |research share − DALY share|. Each level-2 cause contributes ½ of its absolute share gap; level-1 bars sum these cause
contributions, including within-group differences. The three sections are alternative views of the same decomposition; do not add across sections. Research shares are
normalised study–cause links across all 22 GBD level-2 causes, including all three injury causes. Base: 518 eligible disease-coded LMIC records in 2010–2012 and 2,005 in
2021–2023, from 41,610 included records. Unspecified infection/injury codes are excluded here because they lack a level-2 assignment; no smoothing or minimum-count filter
is used. DALYs are summed across 2021–2023; rows within each level-1 group follow pooled LMIC DALYs across 2010–2023. Intervals use 1,000 within-year study bootstrap
resamples; DALY uncertainty is not propagated. Colour indicates the estimated direction; intervals crossing zero mean the change is uncertain.
